intent: Let a user show or hide one section of content in place, with the open state held on the root.
typical_uses: One section of secondary content a user reveals on demand, under a trigger that stays visible

dont_use_when.situation: Several sections, each under its own header, opened independently or one at a time
Content that floats over the page next to the control that opens it, instead of pushing the layout below it down
Switching between alternative panels where exactly one is always shown

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
`disabled` on the root makes a CollapsibleTrigger that passes no `disabled` of its own ignore clicks, Enter and Space; the trigger stays rendered and focusable.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pair `open` with `onOpenChange` and write the next value back, or drop both and use `defaultOpen` - a controlled root with no change handler never receives the trigger's toggle, so the panel never opens or closes

a11y.by: The primitive's Collapsible.Root holds the open state its Collapsible.Trigger reflects in `aria-expanded` and, while open, `aria-controls` naming the panel's id; collapsible.test.tsx asserts the trigger is found by role button under its caption and that the panel is absent until opened

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a function called with the next open value and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape (a reason, the triggering native event, and controls to cancel the change or allow it to propagate), which only tsc can check.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the root carries no class from collapsible.module.css, so nothing of the kit's own styling rides on it.

good.title: Uncontrolled, starting closed
good.code:
<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger>What is included?</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>Everything in the base plan, plus priority support.</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>

bad.title: A stack of Collapsibles standing in for an accordion
bad.why: Each root holds only its own open state, so the sections cannot coordinate (one open at a time) and share no keyboard navigation between their headers. A set of headed sections is an `Accordion`.

onOpenChange.description: TS: ((open: boolean, eventDetails: CollapsibleRootChangeEventDetails) => void) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. onOpenChange is a function called with the next open value and event details, not a value. A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape (a reason, the triggering native event, and controls to cancel the change or allow it to propagate), which only tsc can check.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the root carries no class from collapsible.module.css, so nothing of the kit's own styling rides on it.
